node.title: Re: [OT] SQL "on duplicate key" custom action
node.author: Corion
node.doctext:
I think the "best" approach (if that is supported by your DBMS) are ON UPDATE [https://www.postgresql.org/docs/12/sql-createtrigger.html|triggers], or if that import is a one time thing only, creating a unique key across all columns:

create or replace function skip_insert() returns trigger language plpgsql as $$ begin return null; end $$; create or replace function raise_exception() returns trigger language plpgsql as $$ begin RAISE EXCEPTION 'UPDATE changing row values not allowed'; end $$; CREATE TRIGGER mytrigger ON records INSTEAD OF UPDATE WHEN old.PriKey = new.PriKey and old.Foo=new.Foo and old.Bar=new.Bar FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE PROCEDURE skip_insert() CREATE TRIGGER mytrigger ON records INSTEAD OF UPDATE WHEN old.PriKey = new.PriKey and (old.Foo!=new.Foo or old.Bar!=new.Bar) FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE PROCEDURE raise_exception()

... but this approach does not handle NULL values.
